I’m a master’s student in Management Science at Tongji University, where I work with Professor Chao Zhang. I study how urban infrastructure and public services shape household environmental behavior.
My main project examines whether access to neighborhood recycling stations is associated with household waste-sorting behavior in Ningbo, China. I work with longitudinal operational records from smart recycling bins and am preparing the manuscript with collaborators.
I developed and maintain SECFC, an open-source R package that estimates carbon footprints from lifestyle survey responses. I built the package and its documentation website to help researchers calculate the emissions associated with the behaviors they study.
My other work includes a meta-analysis of carbon labeling and consumer choices, currently under major revision at PNAS Nexus. I also work with Kristian Steensen Nielsen on a project on personal climate agency, contributing to data analysis and visualization.
I’m seeking PhD opportunities beginning in Fall 2027.

title: Community Fieldwork in Ningbo
text:
In January 2025, I visited residential communities in Ningbo to understand how the recycling program operated in practice. I interviewed community staff, property-management personnel, residents, smart-bin supervisors, and collection drivers.
Seeing the system in use helped me understand how the data were generated and led me to consider how access might shape participation.

title: Environmental Systems Engineering Summer School
text: The six-day program at Northeast Normal University focused on AI-driven environmental innovation and brought together more than 80 participants in nine teams. I received the Outstanding Participant award.

title: Oral Presentation at the Chinese Industrial Ecology Academic Annual Conference
text: In July 2025, I gave an oral presentation titled “Bin to Behavior: Characterizing Household Waste-Sorting Behavior Using High-Frequency Disposal Data” at the Chinese Industrial Ecology Academic Annual Conference.

title: Research Experience
text:
Role: Master’s researcher Principal investigator: Chao Zhang, my master’s supervisor Project: World Bank-financed China Plastic Waste Reduction Project, Ningbo Component Period: 2024–present Status: Manuscript in preparation

Within the project, I analyze operational data from smart recycling bins in Ningbo’s central urban area to assess program implementation. My work includes cleaning and structuring longitudinal records, measuring household participation and infrastructure access, and examining how usage varies across locations and over time.
For an associated working paper, I use a research sample drawn from the broader project database to study how spatial friction shapes household use of recycling infrastructure. I have led the paper from developing the research question through data preparation, analysis, visualization, and drafting the initial manuscript.
The underlying operational records are confidential, so I do not share disaggregated data or results on this website.
Fieldwork note
